rapport_notes: Warm, empathetic, acknowledges prior relationship positively, natural conversational flow, good recovery when customer raised prior damage issue.
process_discipline_notes: Rep did not hold silence after 'does that feel fair' or equivalent, and no rate-lock framing at close; however, no differentiator was repeated across stages.

evidence_quotes.agenda: Bri: 'and do you have any questions or concerns specifically that you would like answered on this call about the move.' [Asked after logistics probing had already begun: 'I was just calling in regards to the online booking...']
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised table damage concern: Bri acknowledged and noted it ('I did just put in our notes that the table got damaged in the last move, please ask how to move it'). Customer also mentioned heavy dresser, mechanical bed, TVs, mirrors — Bri asked follow-up on TV size ('do you know what size those are by chance?') and asked about fragile items separately ('do we have anything fragile? Like, large TVs mirrors?'). Two-layer follow-up occurred on damage sensitivity and on the nature/size of fragile items.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Estimate is a window: 'typical move this size takes two movers, one truck between six to eight hours...just because we're kind of unaware of the walk at the second location' [personalizes to walk distance unknown at destination]. Beats it, pay less: 'if they get it done, you know, in a minimal amount of time, you only pay for the amount of time that year there' [15-min increment structure implied in 'time is Perm in fifteen minute increments']. Self-prep tip: 'the most important one is how well prepared you are when we get there. If you do have time to take some of the smaller things over yourself and a car load or two that would really help eat the time down' [customer confirms understanding and commitment to do this]. Missing: no 'we commit to the rate' / 100k-moves framing; no 'does that feel fair' + silence before close; no rate-lock mentioned at close.

top_strength: Brianne expertly uncovered and validated the customer's specific concern (prior table damage) early, showed empathy, and integrated it into move notes rather than dismissing it—building trust with a repeat customer who had already experienced a service recovery.
coaching_note: Add the quid-pro-quo framing at the very top ('let me ask a few questions so I can get you an accurate quote'), ask the agenda line *before* confirming pickup address and logistics, and close with explicit rate-lock language ('your rate locks when you book') plus a clear ask ('would you like our help with your move?') rather than just an open offer to call/email if questions arise.
